research_questions.statement: Can a neural optimal transport framework (CellOT) learn single-cell perturbation responses from unpaired control and perturbed populations?

provenance.text_excerpt: Based on recent developments in neural optimal transport18, CellOT learns an optimal transport map for each perturbation in a fully parameterized and highly scalable manner.

claims.statement: CellOT learns a fully parameterized transport map that can be applied to unseen samples.

provenance.text_excerpt: Instead of directly learning a transport map19–21, CellOT parameterizes a pair of dual potentials with input convex neural networks22. This choice induces an important theory-motivated inductive bias essential to model stability18.

claims.statement: Parameterizing dual potentials with input convex neural networks induces a theory-motivated inductive bias essential to model stability.

experiments_or_tasks: Learning a map T_k from unperturbed control population ρ_c to perturbed population ρ_k using optimal transport.
Parameterizing dual potentials with input convex neural networks to recover the optimal map via gradient of a convex function.

methods.name: CellOT
methods.protocol_description: CellOT learns an optimal transport map for each perturbation by parameterizing dual potentials with input convex neural networks. The map T_k is recovered as the gradient of a convex function g_k (∇g_k). This approach avoids direct parameterization of the primal map and provides an inductive bias for stability.
